C · What one sub-layer does to x
Two ways of measuring "how much did this sub-layer change x"
"It adds" is the length of what the sub-layer adds, and "added ÷ x" compares it with the x it is added to. "Direction kept" is the cosine between x before and after the step:
means x still points the same way, lower means the sub-layer turned it. Post-LN sub-layers turn x much more; Pre-LN sub-layers nudge it.
The length of what each sub-layer reads and adds, and how far it turns x
What to take from section C
In Post-LN every sub-layer reads x at full strength and its output is added to an x of the same size, so each step turns x a lot (direction kept
on average). In Pre-LN each sub-layer reads a normalised copy (always
long) and adds to an x that is already longer, so each step turns x less (
each layer rewrite more; Pre-LN makes each layer a gentler correction, which is more stable — and, in very deep stacks, can leave later layers with less and less influence (section D).

The cost of Pre-LN: later layers matter less
Pre-LN pays for its stability with growth. x gets longer with every block (
for Post-LN), while each block still adds an update of about the
same size, so each later block moves x relatively less: its update shrinks from
large length, which is why the gradient reaching the top blocks shrinks (
). Smaller early updates are part of why Pre-LN trains without warm-up;
relatively weak later layers are the price, and research on large pre-norm models reports deep layers that contribute surprisingly little.
E · Pros and cons, side by side
measured on this page where marked · otherwise from the published research

A typical summary gets the direction right. These are the places where it is imprecise, measured against section D and the research it rests on.

Post-LN normalises x itself after every addition: x stays the same size, every layer keeps full influence, but the skip route is divided at every step and training deep stacks needs care (warm-up, lower learning rates). Pre-LN normalises only the copy each sub-layer reads: the skip route stays intact and training is much more forgiving, but
x grows with depth, a final
is required, and later layers matter less. For a
model like this notebook both train fine;
switched because Pre-LN is the arrangement that keeps working as models get deeper.
